description: Soy Keler, estudiante de Ingeniería de Sistemas (5º semestre) en la CUN, Colombia. Manejo HTML, CSS y JavaScript básico, y uso IA como apoyo para programar. Participo de forma individual en el reto "Space Mission Design Game": un juego web donde se diseña y simula una misión espacial con recursos limitados. Es mi primer hackathon. Meta: entregar un juego simple y terminado.
summary: Orbit One: Mission Designer is a browser game where you design, launch and operate a small satellite. You are the Mission Designer. You pick 3 of 4 engineers, build a 3U CubeSat with real limits of 4 kg and $300,000, and fly a mission in four phases: launch, power, contact and science. The engineer you leave out becomes the narrator in Mission Control. A better part can do a missing engineer's job, but you can only afford one, so there are four ways to win and none is perfect. Before each decision the game teaches the science with a short lesson, and the player must work out the answer. Students rarely get to try a whole mission from start to finish. This game lets them try, fail, read why, and try again.
details:
Play: https://palenciakeler.github.io/MissionDesigner/
Code: https://github.com/palenciakeler/MissionDesigner

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS Orbit One:
Mission Designer is a browser game. You design, launch and operate a 3U CubeSat that must reach a 400 km orbit and take images of Earth.
1. Briefing. Elena, the Mission Director, explains the mission and what a CubeSat is.
2. Team. You pick 3 of 4 engineers: launch, power, communications and science. The fourth goes to Mission Control and narrates the mission.
3. Build. You choose a rocket, solar panels, an antenna and instruments. Each has a basic and a better version. Three live meters show budget, mass and power. If one is over the limit, the mission cannot start.
4. Mission. Four phases. Before each one, the engineer for that topic gives a short lesson with a metaphor. Then you decide.
- Launch: set speed and angle. The orbit is simulated step by step with Newton's gravity. Too slow and it reenters. Too fast and it escapes. The push must be horizontal.
- Power: point the solar panels. Power depends on the angle to the Sun.
- Contact: choose when to send data. A ground station sees the satellite only a few minutes per pass. - Science: point the camera at the target.
5. Report. It says how far the mission got, why, and what to change. It gives 0 to 5 stars

BENEFITS

- It shows a whole mission, not one isolated topic.

- Every decision has a visible cost in budget, mass or power.

- The game does not give the answers. The player uses the formula and the hints.

- Failure teaches: the report explains the cause.

INTENDED IMPACT

Students rarely get to try a complete mission from concept to operation. This game is for them. It runs in any browser, with no install and no account, so a teacher can use it in one class. The goal is that a student finishes a game understanding why real missions are made of trade-offs.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

- The engineer you leave out becomes your narrator. The cost of your choice has a face and a voice.

- A better part can cover a missing engineer, but you can only afford one. So there are four ways to win and none is perfect.

- Each engineer has a personality and teaches their own phase.

- The launch is not a quiz. The player sets speed and angle and watches real orbital physics decide.

FACTORS CONSIDERED
- Scientific validity: every limit and formula comes from a NASA source. Simplifications are declared in the game and in the repository.
- Scope: one mission done well, with a fixed 400 km orbit, instead of many shallow options.
- Accessibility: simple English, short texts, and lessons before each decision for players with no space background.
- Honesty about AI: all AI use is declared in the code, the images and the video.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks. Canvas for the orbit simulation. GitHub and GitHub Pages. Claude (Anthropic) for coding assistance. Google Gemini for images. ElevenLabs for the video narration. HyperFrames for the video.

NEXT STEPS More orbits and destinations, random events, and a team mode for up to four players, one per role.
